purpose: Determine whether execution stops inside the MSR TTBR1_EL1 / ISB pair by writing two markers that do not depend on the new page table

why_markers_are_identity_mapped.observation: stage 47 (entry to set_mmu_ttb_alternate) is written; stage 49 (set_mmu_ttb) never is
why_markers_are_identity_mapped.deduction: The five instructions from the return landing point to the next wrapper are mapped and executable and touch only mapped __DATA_CONST, so control never reaches them: the switch does not return.
why_markers_are_identity_mapped.key_fact: Each of those four instructions is fetched through TTBR1; the ISB makes the new table effective for the very next fetch. A marker in __DATA or in compiled C code would be fetched through the table under test and would inherit the exact fault being investigated.
why_markers_are_identity_mapped.solution: Store the markers through the low-half 1:1 bootstrap map. The switch writes TTBR1 only, so TTBR0 still translates the low half identically on both sides of the MSR. The stores therefore survive a broken new table.

marker_design.location: top page of the 2 GiB bootstrap window 0x8c0000000..0x940000000, above topOfKernelData and above the new page tables, so no kernel allocation uses it
marker_design.gate: TB710FU_SWITCH_MARKS=1 on the boot command line; a stock boot runs the original call
marker_design.stub: single literal asm block, because an equivalent C version with two volatile byte stores compiled to 'sturb w9, [x8, #-1]' with the constant hoisted ahead of the barriers

in_kernel_machine_code.note: the probed function was inlined, so there is no symbol; the sequence was located by its distinctive movz/movk immediates in __TEXT_EXEC

verification.patch_series: 0001..0007 apply in order; 0007 also applies alone; 0006 and 0007 touch the same file but disjoint line ranges

payload.boot_args: -v serial=3 ramoops=0xac340000 ramoops_size=0x40000 ramoops_ecc=0 ramoops_panic_delay=15 ramoops_reset_after=120 TB710FU_SWITCH_MARKS=1

boundary: Diagnostic image, not a functional fix and not hardware acceptance.
